records.c: Build the shape number from the actor's animation selector. On a rare random result adjust Y by toggling bit one. The selector chooses left or right motion by one pixel, with a screen-boundary test.
Initialize the slot counter to seven when its current shape is zero. Refresh the base shape and use a random test to choose between the ordinary drift and the state-change path.
Move X one unit toward $20 when left of Arthur and toward $90 otherwise. Move Y toward $44 while between $44 and $BF, and increment it outside that interval.
Use a five-bit random value. Results below four set type $3F with a delay of $14, while values four through seven set type $3E. Otherwise prepare the arc if the actor is close enough horizontally.

Compare the horizontal distance to Arthur against $40 and save the distance when closer. Save the starting Y and choose the vertical amplitude from another random test and the vertical distance. Pick the angle step and start angle from the side of Arthur, save Arthur's X as the centre and advance the actor type.
Twenty-four per-slot horizontal centres used during the arc. $87EB stores Arthur's X here when starting the arc.
Twenty-four per-slot vertical centres. Arc setup stores the initial actor Y here. Type $3E reuses the same field for its target Y.
Compute the arc coordinates from the current angle, amplitudes and per-slot centres. Add the angle step and return to the previous actor type when the angle masked with $7F reaches $40.
Enter the resident overlap handler at $397F with Y set to two.
Set the target Y to Arthur's Y minus $15. Move vertically by a pixel toward it, then restore type $3C and try the arc setup once it is reached.
Decrement the countdown. In the range five through fourteen, choose shape $85 and try starting a linked type $40 actor when no such slot is active.
Pick shapes $86 and $87 using bit three of the phase counter at $BC.
Use bits two and three of $BC for shape $88 through $8B, then jump to the resident motion helper.

Compare the parent actor's X with Arthur's X and divide the result into three distance bands. Load the corresponding entry from $88F2 and call the resident linked actor allocator with type $40 and Y set to two.
Three horizontal motion values chosen from the signed distance to Arthur in the type $40 spawn path.
Thirty-two glyph codes spell WIGAN RUGBY LEAGUE FOOTBALL CLUB, the same text at the same address as in stage one. Spaces use $3E.
Set shape $52, a counter of four and a delay of $40. Advance the actor type to $2D and continue into its update.
Check actor bounds and take the current facing bit from the shape. Decrement the turn delay and either sample terrain or pick a new facing and delay.
Toggle the shape low bit. Pick one of four turn delays from $18 through $48 in steps of $10.

Sample terrain 21 pixels below the actor, restore the original Y coordinate, then test the resulting map pointer and tile properties. Use the facing bit and the adjacent attributes to choose a horizontal adjustment.
Combine the two phase bits in $BC with base shape $52 and the facing bit. Enter the common hit-counter handler with Y set to two.
Enter the common hit-counter handler with Y set to $0B.

Use the flags to index two step tables. Horizontal movement subtracts the step below shape $9C and adds it from $9C onward. Apply the vertical step and refresh the sprite descriptor operands before checking bounds.
Use the low phase bit to select alternating values for four resident sprite descriptor bytes.
Three horizontal step magnitudes indexed by the active slot's flags.
Three signed vertical step values indexed by the same flags.

Give the parent a counter of seven. Allocate its type $68 companion, save the companion slot in $196C and advance the parent type. Start the movement countdown and choose the initial horizontal direction by comparing X with Arthur's X.
If Arthur is at or to the right of the parent and his actor type is zero, call the resident interaction helper at $3FDE.
Use the side of Arthur to select the parent and companion facing and use phase bits to animate the companion. Age the spawn timer.
When the delay expires, call $8B12 with a parameter determined by the horizontal distance to Arthur. Drop the new slot 16 pixels when its flags are zero.
Occasionally start a new timer. Move the parent and companion together horizontally. Reverse the step and choose a fresh delay when the movement countdown expires.
Run the parent's hit-counter check. If its type changed from $67, mark the companion inactive.
Select a shape from $6C/$6D or $9C/$9D using the caller's facing and the incoming parameter. Allocate a type $31 actor and install that shape.
Start initialization with shape $ED. The alternate entry starts with shape $EC.
Set type $6B, initialize the slot's counter and flags, allocate a linked type $30 slot and give the linked slot six hits.
Check the linked type $30 slot before animation. If it has changed type, retire this slot and decrement $8C81. A zero counter tail-calls the terrain writer with pattern selector $0B.
When the slot flags and phase permit it, choose a target pose from $8C64 with a random or distance-derived index. Move one step toward that pose while preserving the shape's low bit.
With zero flags, age the delay. On expiry choose a new delay, and at a qualifying random value allocate a type $31 actor through the linked slot and shift the result down 16 pixels.
Use the current pose number including the facing bit to look up X and Y offsets. Place the linked slot relative to the parent and set its shape to $F6 or $F7.
Four candidate pose indexes selected by $8BD5.
Five parameters passed to $8B12, indexed by the pose without its facing bit.
Ten signed horizontal offsets for the linked slot indexed by pose and facing.
Ten signed vertical offsets paired with the horizontal table.
Set to two by $95A2. A type $6B update decrements it when the linked type $30 slot disappears. When it reaches zero the update passes selector $0B to the terrain-column writer.
Advance type and set the hit counter to six. Seed the angle, clear its motion state and use the horizontal difference from Arthur to initialize the projection distance.
Patch two resident descriptor bytes according to which side Arthur is on and animate between shapes $F8 and $F9. Select the projection path from the slot's motion state.
Follow a projection centred on Arthur's X and a saved Y. With distance at least $38, step the actual coordinates toward the projection. At shorter distances move the projection radius toward $2A.
At radius $2A a phase and random gate can enter one of two alternate motion states. The second path initializes a separate angle increment and ramp direction.
State one uses added angle steps and decreases the distance at angle boundaries. State two recentres on Arthur and ramps an additional angle step up and down.
Run the common hit check with parameter $0B after updating the position.
The three signed X steps chosen by comparing the slot's X with its projected X.
The three signed Y steps chosen by comparing the slot's Y with its projected Y.
Twenty-four horizontal origin bytes indexed by actor slot, updated from Arthur's X.
Twenty-four vertical origin bytes indexed by slot, used by the vertical projection.
Twenty-four additional angle increments used by the second motion state.
Twenty-four flags controlling whether the extra angle increments rise or fall.
Advance the angle by two and calculate X and Y using the resident projection helpers and this slot's saved origin.
Advance type, set the hit count and saved hit operand to $14, choose shape $FA and start the randomized delay.
While the slot's state is zero, animate two shapes and move Y one unit toward the target at $904E. A negative flag at $E9 updates the target from Arthur's height.
At eligible countdown and random values, offset the slot coordinates, spawn type $40 and restore both coordinates.
Run the resident hit check and advance through $3397 once the actor's type drops below $6E.
Save the hit count and make the slot temporarily invulnerable. Change its shape and coordinates, initialize the 64-step trail and allocate four type $75 followers with staggered delays.
Move by the signed X operand and the current Y step. Store each coordinate in its trail buffer. Use the delay and remaining path length to move through the successive Y steps.
Exclusive OR with $FC reverses the signed step between plus two and minus two each time the trail starts.
End the trail, restore the hit count and undo the initial offsets. Choose the delay for the next trail.
Holds the hit count saved as the trail begins. The slot restores it from this immediate operand.
Keep an offscreen position until the delay expires. Then copy successive X and Y values from the two trail buffers and retire after index $3F.
Toggle the shape low bit when the phase is zero under mask three.
Five signed vertical steps for successive portions of the trail.
Base values added to the random delay when stepping into the next trail phase.
Saved target Y approached by the actor before it begins a trail.
Starts at $40 and decrements as each coordinate pair is written to the trail buffers.
Sixty-four recorded X positions read by the trailing actors.
Sixty-four recorded Y positions paired with the X positions.
At zero delay, a random gate can change the slot to type $70 and spawn type $72. Set the animation base then continue into the shared motion.

Enter with animation base $B6. With time left, apply the signed slot steps when either is nonzero. If both are zero, increment Y and refresh the shape through $9205. Expiry enters the path-table phase at $916A.
The high operand of the increment at $9121. The following call updates the shape using the current animation base.
On a qualifying random result set vertical speed three, derive the delay from Arthur's relative height and select a signed horizontal step by comparing their positions.
Move up and animate. On eligible phases choose X and Y offsets from the path tables. At selected steps the random and proximity gates can restart directional motion or enter the descent.
Select vertical step minus five and derive a delay from height and a random value before changing the slot to type $71.
Apply the resident coordinate helpers and place any linked slot two X units right and thirteen Y units down. Then run the hit check.
Add the two selected phase bits to the base shape in $12 and store the result.
Forty signed horizontal steps indexed by the path counter.
Forty signed vertical steps paired with the X steps.
Select shape $BA through the resident shape setter.
Advance the actor type, clear the hit counter and motion flag, assign a phase index and save the original X position.
The starting index installed in each slot. The initializer increments the operand by two for the next slot.
Retire below row $20. On delay expiry advance the phase modulo sixteen and toggle the motion flag. When active, select an X offset and shape, then move by two in the direction chosen by that shape.
Two X offsets from the slot's saved anchor, selected with a random bit.
Two shapes paired with the X offsets. Shape $6D moves left and the other moves right.
Sixteen delays selected by the actor's phase index.

Select four or five for $35CA according to $FD. At $FD=$2F and $FB at least $3C, advance the stage section and reinitialize scrolling. Before column $31, a free condition at $B7 and a random test can allocate another actor.
Require an empty optional actor count and a one-in-32 random mask match. Allocate a slot, choose a vertical offset near Arthur and set actor type $3A with one of two sides and initial shapes.
Two possible horizontal start positions selected by the low random bit at $9349.
In the first seven coarse rows call $35CA with selector four, or five at row three. Set $B903 to $80 below horizontal coordinate $98 and $82 from there onward.
Write the section scroll flag at $4728. Set it from horizontal coordinate $98 onward, or below $61 while the coarse row is below $1A.
Copy six bytes from one of the two $940D rows into $4F56. Select the second row for horizontal coordinates below $61.
At vertical row $25 call $2EEF with bank one. Above $25 call it with bank zero.
This jump skips the temporary placement scan. Writing opcode $2C here turns it into a BIT instruction that falls through to $93CA.

At horizontal coordinate $72 or above, test for actor $67 through $3DD6. If carry is clear, use $93D8 to decide whether to install the temporary placement record and call $30BA. When the counter becomes negative, restore the jump at $93C7 and install the regular list at $9586.
Immediate operand of the load at $93D7. Zero suppresses the extra placement call. The decrement at $93E6 restores the jump and regular placement pointer when the counter goes negative.
Enter $9419 while horizontal coordinate is below $96 and row is below $10. Return directly outside that rectangle.
One six-byte placement for type $66 followed by the two-byte terminator. The temporary scan at $93DB points $B1/$B2 here.
Two six-byte presets copied over $4F56 by $93AF. The second preset consists of six $FF bytes.

Use the entry at $1F29 indexed by the current X, two random tests and the active optional actor count to gate allocation. Place type $71 or $70 at Y=$22 and one of 32 equally spaced X positions, with an initial shape of $B6.
Replace the immediate values in the resident shape handling routines with $49 through $4E and four copies of $34.

Save the pattern selector from X. For each of six destinations, resolve the chunk pointer and add a row offset and column offset. Use the selector table at $94EA to find the first replacement tile, then write down the column in steps of 20 bytes. Stop at $FF or after four writes.
Twelve offsets into the pattern bytes at $9508. The saved selector in $16 moves down by one per destination.
Six even selectors into the resident chunk pointer table at $4CF0.
Six offsets to add to the row displacements before writing the replacement tiles.
Six indexes into the row-displacement table at $1BD6.
Replacement tile indices read by $94D3. A value of $FF ends the writes for a destination early.

Section 08 has 17 ordered spawn records. Each six-byte record contains a 16-bit X tile, a 16-bit Y tile, packed sub-tile offsets and the actor ID. The scan at $30B3 advances after allocating the actor.

Section 09 has 8 ordered spawn records. Each six-byte record contains a 16-bit X tile, a 16-bit Y tile, packed sub-tile offsets and the actor ID. The scan at $30B3 advances after allocating the actor.
Two $FF bytes end the four-record actor list at $9586. Two zero bytes separate that terminator from the setup routine at $95A2.
Section 08 and 09 has 0 optional spawn positions. Each record holds the two tile coordinates and one packed sub-tile byte. The bounded search at $3175 tests visibility and a random condition.

Set the scroll origin, patch resident shape selectors and three overlay operands, and set $9273 to $FF. Apply terrain-column pattern five and change the jump at $93C7 to BIT so the frame hook can scan the temporary placement. Then tail-call $2FCD with the terrain patch list at $95D1.
Ten terrain edit records consumed by $2FCD. Each gives a chunk pointer selector, column and row offsets, a count minus one, and the replacement tile bytes. A negative selector ends the script.
Three little-endian start addresses for stage 5 music. The resident stage setter copies the six bytes into index six of the SID song table.
Stage 5 supplies this starting address for voice 1 of in-game track six. The command stream includes notes, control changes and calls to shared phrases.
Stage 5 supplies this starting address for voice 2 of in-game track six. The command stream includes notes, control changes and calls to shared phrases.
Stage 5 supplies this starting address for voice 3 of in-game track six. The command stream includes notes, control changes and calls to shared phrases.
Continuation of the stage 5 tune region. Following command targets from its three starting pointers reaches the last phrase bytes at $9E06.
Zero-filled end of the loaded stage music window through $9FFF. Terrain chunk entries start after the $A000 page boundary.
Loaded 32-byte prefix before the first 200-byte terrain chunk. The entry snapshots share byte $55 followed by zeros. Layout pointers start at $A020.

Loaded 200-byte storage at terrain chunk pointer index 27. The resident stage 5 layout selects only indices below 27.
Use the tile code as the index into the $B6 page selected by $2EEF. $48CC subtracts the selected byte from the player's ground-aligned Y value.
Surface offsets for the other terrain bank. $2EEF loads $B7 as the page for the pointer at $C4/$C5.
Tile properties for the first terrain bank. $3C29 maps nearby character-screen positions through this table and stores the attribute bytes at $EE-$F5.
Second terrain bank's tile attributes. $2EEF selects page $B9 for the pointer at $C2/$C3.

The second terrain-property page starts at $B900. The stage hook writes this entry for character code three at $9389. The rest of the page is read through the same terrain-property pointer at $C2/$C3.
Colour lookup by terrain character code. The first bank case in $2EEF selects this page for $4BF8.
Colour lookup by terrain character code. The second bank case in $2EEF patches $4BF8 to this page.
Top-left character codes indexed by the tile number. $5010 and $5027 read this page.
Top-right character codes paired with the left half by $4FF6. $5016 and $5031 read this page.
Bottom-left character codes for the lower half of each tile. $5057 and $506E read this page.
Bottom-right character codes for the lower half of each tile. $505D and $5078 read this page.
Eleven 64-byte VIC sprite slots starting at pointer $20. These slots match in all five stage images and render projectile silhouettes and small circular effects.

Stage sprite slots at pointers $2B through $97. Includes the stage enemy figures, stacked large-actor pieces and the end of the common effects set. The 64th byte of each slot is outside the 24 by 21 pixel raster.
Start of sprite 3B in stage 5. The VIC reads 21 rows of three bytes per slot and advances the base by 64 bytes.
Start of sprite 40 in stage 5. The VIC reads 21 rows of three bytes per slot and advances the base by 64 bytes. The VIC sees these shapes in RAM beneath the CPU I/O window.
Start of sprite 50 in stage 5. The VIC reads 21 rows of three bytes per slot and advances the base by 64 bytes. The VIC sees these shapes in RAM beneath the CPU I/O window.
Start of sprite 60 in stage 5. The VIC reads 21 rows of three bytes per slot and advances the base by 64 bytes. The VIC sees these shapes in RAM beneath the CPU I/O window.
Start of sprite 70 in stage 5. The VIC reads 21 rows of three bytes per slot and advances the base by 64 bytes. The VIC sees these shapes in RAM beneath the CPU I/O window.
Start of sprite 80 in stage 5. The VIC reads 21 rows of three bytes per slot and advances the base by 64 bytes.
Offset 29 of sprite 83 in the stage 5 art. The VIC sees this RAM as part of a graphics slot.
Start of sprite 90 in stage 5. The VIC reads 21 rows of three bytes per slot and advances the base by 64 bytes.
Offset 26 of sprite 96 in the stage 5 art. The VIC sees this RAM as part of a graphics slot.
Eight sprite slots starting at pointer $98. These match in all five graphics loads. The rendered slots include small burst and narrow upright shapes.
The second terrain character set. Its 256 eight-byte glyphs are selected by the $0A entry at $5D87 in the terrain bank table.
Stage 5 terrain charset at E800, glyph 80, row 0. The bytes are VIC pixel rows for the terrain cells. Eight bytes form one character.
The first terrain character set. Its 256 eight-byte glyphs are selected by the $0C entry at $5D86 in the terrain bank table.
Stage 5 terrain charset at F000, glyph 7A, row 5. The bytes are VIC pixel rows for the terrain cells. Eight bytes form one character.
Stage 5 terrain charset at F000, glyph B5, row 7. The bytes are VIC pixel rows for the terrain cells. Eight bytes form one character.
Stage 5 terrain charset at F000, glyph BA, row 2. The bytes are VIC pixel rows for the terrain cells. Eight bytes form one character.
Stage 5 terrain charset at F000, glyph C8, row 2. The bytes are VIC pixel rows for the terrain cells. Eight bytes form one character.
Stage 5 terrain charset at F000, glyph E0, row 4. The bytes are VIC pixel rows for the terrain cells. Eight bytes form one character.
